![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

In `downstreamBlockers`, `receiptRow?.blockers` is processed manually using `String(blocker)`. This can be simplified and made safer by passing `receiptRow` directly into `rowBlockerIds` along with the other rows. `rowBlockerIds` already handles both string blockers and object blockers (via `blocker_id`) safely, avoiding potential `"[object Object]"` stringification if `receiptRow?.blockers` ever contains objects.

```suggestion
  const blockers = rowBlockerIds(visualRow, figureRow, receiptRow, rightsRow, qrmRow);
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When passing metadata to gating or normalization functions, preserve the metadata in its object form instead of stringifying it, to ensure nested fields can be properly inspected.
</details>

Fixed in 78295051f. `downstreamBlockers` now passes `receiptRow` through `rowBlockerIds`, so string blockers and `{ blocker_id }` object blockers use the same normalization path. Added a regression test that object-shaped receipt blockers are preserved and do not become `[object Object]`.
